decisions.statement: Nothing here loads a check.
A selector says the input a check takes.
Which page types are changes is read from what each page type extends.
A page type extending a change through another page type is a change too.
A body read as code is named `.ts` or `.tsx`.
A body read as a stylesheet is named `.css`.
A check judging both reaches code and stylesheets through one selector.
A selector takes as input every path the selector hands over.
Whether a change holds the input a check takes is answered here.
A runner carrying an input is run only over a change holding a path it takes.
A selector names a path before reading it, so a path it drops is never opened.
A selector over texts is told the index the change leaves as well as the path.
The page an entry file sits beside is answered here.
Which section names an entry file is read from the index rather than listed here.
The page an entry file sits beside is composed out of that file's own name.
A page composed that way is answered only where that page is there to read.
A selector over pages and their entry files takes both as input.
A check judging a path the change takes away walks the change itself.
A body that is there and will not open refuses the check reading that body.
A refusal for a body that will not open names the path that body is at.
A path nothing sits at reads as nothing rather than as unreadable.
A path a folder sits at reads as nothing.
A folder has no body a check judges.
Git tracks the link a package is reached by.
That link leads to a folder.
A walk over everything takes the files in the tree rather than the files the index names.
Which files those are is git's walk rather than a listing of the tree on disk.
A listing of the tree names neither a link nor a path only the index holds.
A walk over everything names both, so a check judging either sees it.
A root that is no tree refuses the walk rather than taking nothing.
A body is opened rather than looked for and then opened.
A body that is not text refuses the check reading that body.
A refusal for a body that is not text names the path that body is at.
An audit reading each text in the tree reads that text through this module.
A check refusing a body that is not text reads that body through this module.
A check reading a body leniently reaches `body-text` rather than this module.
A change held over a run reads each path once and answers from that read.
A path taken away after that read is answered with the body that read got.
A body that will not open refuses the run rather than being held.
The index is no file of the tree's, however git holds it, and is walked by nothing.
A selector over bodies is told the index the change leaves as well as the path.
A selector hands each body over as it is read rather than reading every body first.
A change naming no path is what a run judging the whole tree is opened with.
Such a change walks nothing, so a run wanting no walk pays for none.
The pages of named types are collected by searching for the names those pages have.
The index answers those pages far sooner, and is asked for none of them.
An audit judges the tree, so an audit reading the index cannot catch a wrong one.
That search is made by ripgrep, which answers the paths git would answer.
A search a check makes takes one thread, spending no more than one processor.
A search over threads ends sooner and spends more, and a ceiling counts what is spent.
A search finding no page answers no path rather than refusing.
Naming no type collects nothing, and asks for no search.
An audit over the texts holding a spelling is handed those texts by a search.
A text the search leaves out is never opened, so nothing reads or parses it.
The spellings searched for are the ones without which the check refuses nothing.

definition: how a check reaches the text it judges
